tree_state: tool, tests, report, note and matrix edit are committed at the recorded commit; the raw JSON outputs and the dyld disassembly listed under artifacts are local-only (gitignored) and hashed here
summary: Static audit of the owner's iPhone10,3 iOS 16.5 (20F66) userland as unpacked by the donor recipe (IOS-009), against the project kernel tree (xnu-8796.121.2, DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_E1S). All six programs (dyld, launchd, xpcproxy, amfid, backboardd, SpringBoard) are plain arm64 iOS 16.5 Mach-O with chained fixups and LC_LOAD_DYLINKER /usr/lib/dyld; every required library of every closure resolves to an image of the 43-file, 2710-image dyld shared cache (only weak/optional liblinkguard, libobjc-env, Darwinup and MLCompilerRuntime are absent). libsystem_kernel has 506 svc #0x80 sites, 502 with an immediate x16: 474 match the project's syscalls.master / syscall_sw.c table by name, 0 numbers are absent, 0 names differ, 22 are nosys/enosys in this configuration (251-256, 258-265, 293, 337, 418, 419, 483, 493, 519, 535) and 6 stubs have no exported name; dyld's own 158 distinct numbers are all enabled. dyld reads commpage offsets +0xd0, +0xd8, +0x10c (and byte +0x105) that the open header does not define, and two Apple system registers (S3_6_C15_C1_5 in dyld only, S3_4_C15_C10_6 in dyld and libsystem_kernel); the register path of the allocator write protection is guarded by a byte whose origin was not found. dyld embeds libignition (cryptex graft, trust cache load gated by ignition_level); the shared region (0x180000000 + 0xa9eec000) fits the kernel's SHARED_REGION_BASE/SIZE_ARM64. No missing userland file was found for the six programs.
evidence_category: host-test / source-review. Nothing ran on the S24 and nothing ran in an emulator. Static name and number matches are not behaviour matches; commpage and register scans are heuristics that show access shapes, not what the code does. The hand reading of dyld used the Android NDK llvm-objdump 19.0.1 as a viewer and is not reproducible by the tool.

commands.result: OK: planning views match the current registry

limits: Static analysis only. No Apple code ran. Names and numbers agree; semantics, argument layouts and the 122.4~1 vs 121.2 kernel differences were not compared.
Commpage and system-register scans are pattern heuristics over __text (movk/orr address shapes, mrs/msr encodings); a miss proves nothing, a hit proves an access shape.

The origin of the allocator byte (+0x21) that selects the Apple-register write-protection path in dyld was not found; whether the S24 takes that path is unknown until the first dyld run (brk #1 at dyld vm 0x7d3c would show it).
Which of the 22 nosys numbers the six programs call is not established.
The libignition branch with the donor's merged root, the kernel's code-signature registration and entitlement answers, and the cache launchd handshake (R09) are unobserved.
The cache auditor is own code because no ready tool was usable for reading the split cache together with the project kernel tables; the NDK llvm-objdump was used only as a viewer.
